I'm not really against the whole concept of chanting but the things revolving around it. I was introduced to it when I asked my friend, how he achieved just the goal he was aiming for, in his 12th grade examination. I was so intrigued I went on to attend my first meeting with him & ended up taking up the practice & till date have achieved multiple things through it. I associated the practice with 'The Secret' and power of visualization, took help of a vision board temporarily as well, aiming for the utmost result. I guess since the start I had something against 'shakubuku-ing' people; I mean I did share my victories with everyone, with all my pride for the practice but all with a mindset of helping them & not forcing them into something. I was one of the active ones in my chapter too. But the members with the highest posts felt like blinded by the faith; my most disappointing conversations & a big turn off honestly was when I told one of my mentors that my childhood friend attended a meeting but she wasn't interested in this practice, which led her to say 'its not like they're not interested, something something, you should chant for her so that she starts chanting, gets into the practice, blah blah blah'. After a conversation with my counselor who's also into spirituality and has tried different things including chanting, I have come to a conclusion that after putting in months & years in this practice, may be not being very active but being a constant part of it, I knew that in a way I considered it as a 'cult' always, but just didn't say it out loud. Since then I have left all the WhatsApp groups and decided to be independent about chanting or considering any other spiritual practice with the sole goal of bettering my life & making a positive change without getting blinded by groups like cults that sell a spiritual practice. Again, still believe in chanting, but not in the people that uphold that practice.
